items.title: Design optional workspace discovery and central health monitoring
items.problem: Future admin-experience improvements need bounded resource selection and independent optional behavior.
scope: FUTURE.md (link the bounded design; preserve deferred feature completion criteria)
.github/workflows/validate.yml (supported PowerShell guard and declared Pester selection only)
acceptance: Discovery is read-only and requires exact workspace selection; unavailable/cross-tenant targets stop.
Optional health uses deployment-validation or Azure Monitor only for compatible signals.
Sentinel analytics and incident automation stay solution-owned; no forced monitoring dependency or inferred enforcement.
validation: Run focused tests for changed behavior from tests/; fixtures do not prove live-service or endpoint behavior.
evidence: The bounded design maps the current exact tenant, subscription, resource group, workspace and Sentinel onboarding validation, then specifies a future read-only candidate record and selection receipt bound to one canonical ARM workspace ID, target tenant, required tables, capture time and normalized evidence digest. Partial enumeration, cross-tenant, ambiguous, foreign, stale, forbidden, unavailable, failed or digest-mismatched evidence prevents selection; manual entry uses the same checks.

The design limits optional health to compatible point-in-time deployment-validation evidence and existing Azure Monitor data. It distinguishes resource readability, log queryability, Logic App action success, API connection state, recipient receipt and account recovery, and leaves central ownership, thresholds, routing, schedules and deployment for separate administrator authorization.

Existing Sentinel analytics, automation, role assignment, playbook and cleanup ownership remain local and optional. No picker, provider call, environment mutation, permission grant, component adoption, monitor, polling service, infrastructure or runtime change was implemented; FUTURE.md completion criteria remain explicitly open.

Current-source offline validation passed 114/114 Pester tests with supported Pester 5.7.1, Bicep compilation matched the checked-in ARM template, and the Git whitespace check passed. Backlog schema and generated-Markdown checks also passed. The initial local run selected incompatible installed Pester 6.2.0 and failed seven legacy mock assertions; the retained rerun isolated 5.7.1 and passed without source changes.

Independent source-bound design review completed all three original EA-003 discovery criteria. Successful empty queries remain eligible queryability evidence with an ingestion-health warning; unkeyed digests establish internal consistency only, not authenticated capture or deployment authorization. The design accurately maps the current selected-subscription preprovision shortcut and separate deployment-validation tenant check. Existing Sentinel lifecycle stays solution-owned and optional. FUTURE workspace-picker and actual central-health-alert completion criteria remain open.

Registered offline validation passed 114/114 under supported Pester 5.7.1 on PowerShell 7.6.6, with Bicep/checked-in ARM equality; initial installed Pester 6.2.0 legacy-mock failures were retained separately. Canonical backlog schema/render, JSON/links, original criteria and unrelated records, protected runtime/infrastructure/component bytes, and tracked/new-file whitespace passed. Hosted validation now checks 64-bit PowerShell 7.6+ before tests and explicitly imports its declared Pester 5.7.1. This is design completion only: no discovery provider, environment mutation, picker, permission grant, central monitor, notification delivery, recipient receipt or recovery drill was implemented or run.

items.title: HOL Guard rule for `azd down --purge --force`?
items.problem: GitHub issue 20 is external feature outreach for an optional HOL Guard review rule around the documented destructive `azd down --purge --force` command, not a reported repository or Azure Developer CLI defect. Reconcile the current source and active pull requests, then design compatibility, trust, permission, fixture and rollout boundaries before any separately authorized external contribution or enablement.
scope: Paths and trigger cited in the linked issue
acceptance: Classify the report as still reproducible, already fixed, superseded or requiring live evidence; record the exact current revision.
For a reproducible defect, demonstrate the linked trigger with an offline regression and apply the smallest fix preserving tenant/target/ownership and failure semantics.
For a feature, produce a bounded design with compatibility, optional permissions, acceptance and rollout gates before implementation; no live mutation or automatic issue closure.
validation: Read the issue body and current source/PRs; capture the exact reproduction and existing registered offline validation command.
Use deterministic fixtures for the described trigger and negative boundary; retain current-source results. Do not rerun production or tenant operations to reproduce it.
evidence: Read-only reconciliation at repository base 888cbbd0135a116fdf9924135910b08ad56b6a50 classified issue 20 as optional external feature outreach rather than an azd or repository defect. The merged PR 21 changed only the pinned catalog workflow and is unrelated. Current predown behavior retains tenant assertion and exact-owned cleanup refusal semantics; no defect reproduction or live evidence was required for this classification.

The adopted design binds the immutable HOL Extension Builder specification at 1a96f4d9c838b3953b1bcf5725ccefc0d26ff91d. Every positively intercepted, parser-admitted and fixture-proven azd down form must resolve to review with zero target executions and no safeArgv. Rejected, differently parsed or non-intercepted forms are coverage gaps; any generic unknown-command review floor is a separately fixture-proven host-policy property.

The optional external source remains off by default and adds no Azure, ARM, Microsoft Graph or repository permission and no solution runtime dependency. No saved azd help snapshot, HOL tool run, fixture result, implementation, matcher coverage, external contribution, enablement, authentication, provider operation or teardown execution is claimed; each remains separately authorized.

items.title: Validate selected tenant before guided setup
items.problem: A supplied tenant can disagree with the cached selected subscription while preprovision changes environment choices and CLI context; the later bootstrap guard already prevents Graph mutation and ARM deployment, but setup should stop at the earlier boundary.
scope: scripts/Tenant.Guards.psm1 (reuse existing guard; only bounded changes if required)
tests/ (actual validation-script and tenant-guard boundary fixtures)
docs/ (current behavior and backlog tracking only)
acceptance: Reject a known supplied-tenant/selected-subscription mismatch before persistent environment writes, wizard prompts, CLI account selection or downstream resource/workspace setup.
Preserve matching cached-session behavior, authorized subscription selection, missing-tenant resolution and standard broker/browser authentication without device-code fallback.

Reuse the existing tenant-context guard before downstream setup and retain the bootstrap guard; prove through actual-script fixtures that mismatches cause no downstream setup and matching/missing-tenant cases remain valid.
validation: Run focused actual-script and tenant-guard fixtures on PowerShell 7.6 or newer, with fake commands only.
Run the registered offline repository validation and preserve the unchanged Graph, infrastructure, permissions and authentication boundaries.
evidence: Source assessment at main 1113a3ef9666dd8fd4cb45b8cf077f9cca522a82 identified the earlier setup gap. Bootstrap-Tenant still invokes Assert-AzdTenantContext before any Graph request, so no Graph-mutation or ARM-deployment bypass is claimed.

Preprovision now reads the requested subscription and compares its owner tenant with a supplied AZURE_TENANT_ID before `az account set`, azd environment writes, or wizard prompts. After authorized subscription selection, the existing Assert-AzdTenantContext verifies expected, subscription, and active CLI tenant plus active subscription; the original Bootstrap-Tenant guard remains in place.

Actual-script fake-command fixtures prove a supplied mismatch performs one subscription read and then stops with no account selection, login, environment write, or wizard output. Matching cached selection from another active subscription and missing-tenant resolution both complete, with the latter persisting the resolved tenant exactly once. Focused parser and Pester 5.7.1 validation passed 33/33 on PowerShell 7.6.6 without authentication or provider calls.

Registered offline validation passed 118/118 Pester tests with pinned Pester 5.7.1 on PowerShell 7.6.6, Bicep compilation matched the checked-in ARM template, and Git whitespace validation passed. No authentication, provider, Graph, permission, infrastructure, picker, deployment, or resource operation ran.

Independent source review passed all three original criteria. Actual-script fake-command fixtures independently passed 3/3 on PowerShell 7.6.6/Pester 5.7.1; retained author evidence is focused 33/33 and registered offline 118/118 with Bicep/ARM equality. Normal browser login preservation is source-inspected, not live authentication proof. Fresh exact-head hosted validation remains required before merge.
